topic: The Hidden Symmetry: Planar Graph Duality and Euler’s Formula
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Planar Graph
lecture_lines: Planar graphs are drawn without any edges crossing.
They consist of vertices, edges, and faces.
The surrounding exterior area also counts as a face.
This house graph has five vertices and six edges.
Including the exterior, it contains exactly three faces.
animations: Draw two edges crossing, then morph them to be non-crossing.
Draw the 'House' graph and label 5 Vertices in blue (#0000FF).
Highlight 6 Edges in yellow (#FFFF00) and show label 'E'.
Color 3 Faces in green (#00FF00), including the infinite exterior.
Display summary: Planar graphs have non-crossing edges and three components.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic: The Universal Constant
lecture_lines: Euler’s Formula states V minus E plus F equals two.
This value is constant for every connected planar graph.
Adding new components never changes this fundamental result.
Watch this square morph into a complex pentagon.
The real-time counter always stays balanced at two.
animations: Write V - E + F = 2 prominently in white (#FFFFFF).
Display a square graph (V=4, E=4, F=2) and its formula.
Animate the addition of a diagonal edge to the square.
Update the formula to 4 - 5 + 3 = 2 in real-time.
Highlight the constant result '2' with a red (#FF0000) pulse.

sections.title: The Concept of Duality: The Mirror World
lecture_lines: Every planar graph possesses a twin called a dual.
Original faces transform into vertices in the dual world.
Dual edges connect vertices across every original boundary.
animations: Display a planar graph G with 3 regions.
Place a magenta (#FF00FF) dot in every region (face) of G.
Draw cyan (#00FFFF) lines crossing original edges to connect the dots.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Construction of a Dual Graph
lecture_lines: Place a new vertex inside every original face.
Remember to place a vertex in the outer region.
Connect these vertices by crossing every original edge once.
This cube’s dual construction reveals a symmetric octahedron.
Duality exposes the deep links between Platonic solids.
animations: Draw a white (#FFFFFF) wireframe of a 3D cube projection.
Place a red (#FF0000) dot in the center of all 6 faces.
Connect dots in adjacent faces with thick red (#FF0000) lines.
Transition by fading out the white cube wires.
Show the remaining red structure is a perfect octahedron.

sections.title: Mathematical Symmetry and Verification
lecture_lines: Dual graphs swap the roles of vertices and faces.
Both graphs share the exact same number of edges.
This preserves Euler’s characteristic across the transformation.
animations: Display a table: G stats (V:5, E:7, F:4) vs G* stats.
Fill G* stats: V*:4, E*:7, F*:5 showing the reversal.
Compute V* - E* + F* = 2 on screen with highlight.

sections.title: Application: From Map Coloring to Circuit Design
lecture_lines: Duality simplifies problems like the Four Color Theorem.
It helps engineers optimize paths in electrical circuit design.
This hidden symmetry unifies geometry and network logic.
animations: Show a map of countries transforming into a vertex-edge graph.
Show a simple circuit mesh transforming into its nodal dual.
Display closing text 'Symmetry in Structure' in gold (#FFD700).
